article_title: The Model Passed. We Sent a Human to the Road.
boundary: Synthetic evidence only. Figures do not show observed animal movement, crossing use, collision reduction, population response, biodiversity benefit, approval, or a design-ready project.

figures.alt_text: Four evidence cards show 12 of 12 scenarios complete, a 400,000 dollar cost inside a 500,000 dollar cap, 1.603 percent lower modeled effective resistance in the least-favorable safeguard case, and a 47 to 66 percent road-area current change above a 15 percent trigger. An arrow leads to carry forward for feasibility review.
figures.caption: Three favorable checks did not erase the separate road-area review flag. The supported action was further ecological, field, and engineering review—not approval.
figures.forbidden_implication: Observed animal movement, crossing use, ecological benefit, or approval.
figures.question: How can every required connectivity check pass while the overall disposition remains review?
figures.takeaway: A separate road-area diagnostic changed the next action from modeled pass to field review.
figures.title: Why the Ridgeway candidate remained a review

figures.alt_text: Horizontal bars show road-area modeled-current changes of 47.35, 59.59, 65.65, and 64.77 percent for low-barrier, moderate, high-barrier, and future-pressure safeguard scenarios. Every bar lies beyond a dashed 15 percent review line.
figures.caption: The warning did not depend on only one landscape assumption. It appeared in all four safeguard scenarios. The 15% line is an authored synthetic investigation trigger, not a biological threshold.
figures.forbidden_implication: Collision risk, road crossing probability, or animal-use concentration.
figures.question: Was the road-area flag caused by only one safeguard resistance hypothesis?
figures.takeaway: No. The authored 15 percent review trigger was exceeded in all four safeguard scenarios.
figures.title: Road-area diagnostic across safeguard hypotheses

figures.alt_text: Two 20 by 12 synthetic Circuitscape current grids use the same scale. The no-action baseline appears beside the carry-forward candidate. The same road-review cells are outlined in amber. Their summed modeled current changes by 47.35 percent.
figures.caption: Same synthetic landscape, numerical scale, and fixed review area. We summed modeled electrical current inside the outlined cells. We did not observe an animal moving through them.
figures.forbidden_implication: Animal routes, animal-use probability, collision locations, or harm.
figures.question: What spatial evidence produced the low-barrier road-area warning?
figures.takeaway: The 47.35 percent value is the baseline-relative change in a sum over the same 48 fixed cells, not an animal-use prediction.
figures.title: Exact baseline and candidate current maps

figures.alt_text: EcoCorridor Evidence Rail for the controlling safeguard result. It shows the negative 1.60 percent baseline-relative change, exact candidate and baseline matrix jobs, scenario identifier, matrix SHA-256 hash, and accepted numerical QA.
figures.caption: The 1.6031% value has a direct run, baseline, artifact hash, and QA disposition. That makes the calculation auditable. It does not make the ecological assumptions true.
figures.forbidden_implication: Artifact identity as proof of ecological validity.
figures.question: Can a reader reconstruct the controlling 1.6031 percent result?
figures.takeaway: The result resolves to a reducer, candidate and baseline direct jobs, scenario, matrix hashes, and accepted QA.
figures.title: The controlling value's Evidence Rail

figures.alt_text: A six-step flow runs from reviewed inputs to direct Circuitscape runs, local evidence, an optional read-only agent, an unconfirmed draft, and a practitioner. Side branches stop incomplete or QA-rejected evidence before comparison and stop trace or validation failures before a draft. There is no approval arrow.
figures.caption: The agent sits after direct evidence and fixed local checks. It can organize only the approved evidence it receives. Failed evidence creates no comparison or draft, and only a practitioner chooses what to investigate next.
figures.forbidden_implication: Autonomous model changes, ecological judgment, or automatic approval.
figures.question: Where may the agent help, and who still owns the decision?
figures.takeaway: Direct evidence and local validation precede the optional agent; a practitioner owns the next action.
figures.title: The evidence and authority handoff

figures.alt_text: Two nearly equal bars show 10,798 full-context input tokens and 10,542 agent input tokens. A second chart shows a 2.37 percent observed reduction far short of a dashed 25 percent promotion gate.
figures.caption: The agent saved 256 provider-input tokens—2.37%, not the required 25%. The deterministic checklist stayed default.
figures.forbidden_implication: General agent ranking, practitioner usefulness, or adaptive retrieval benefit.
figures.question: Did the historical agent reduce provider context enough to replace the deterministic default?
figures.takeaway: No. It reduced input tokens by 2.37 percent against a predeclared 25 percent gate.
figures.title: Historical Review Brief agent promotion gate
